title: Orphan Claim — Notifier (no Internal) + Parties + Location (Loss → Parties → Location → Summary)
walkthroughSteps: Apply an AC — pushes FNOL state into the orphan path. Land on /fnol/skeleton-create — left nav shows 3 steps (Loss / Parties / Summary)
Fill Client + Reason on the Loss page

walkthroughSteps.title: Notifier type
walkthroughSteps.body: Only Broker or Insured — Internal is deliberately not offered, since internal staff register the claim but are never the notifier themselves. Picking Broker opens the Search broker modal; Insured shows a single free-text input.

walkthroughSteps: Location capture lives on the Loss page itself (2026-09-11, Vasudha feedback — same placement as the regular happy-path flow, not a separate step): 'Add location' opens the manual-entry modal directly — location-picker.component.ts's addLocation() skips the policy-search branch entirely when there's no linked policy, so there's no 'select from contract location' option here. The modal now also offers a GIS address search (type-ahead, independent of any policy) that prefills the manual fields on selection.
Click 'Next' (this page never submits — creation happens on Summary) → /fnol/skeleton-parties, starting empty except for the broker carried over from the notifier screen if one was picked
Optionally 'Add party' (e.g. a different insurer) — parties are never mandatory, Next always works

walkthroughSteps.title: Create
walkthroughSteps.body: Summary reviews Loss, Locations, Parties, and Notifier as read-only cards.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: Registers the skeleton claim and shows a success banner with the new claim ID.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Notifier section uses a Broker / Insured radio — Internal is not offered
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: On the **Loss information** page of the orphan flow, a *radio toggle* picks the notifier type (`Broker` / `Insured`) — only the relevant input renders below. Picking **Broker** opens the *Search broker* modal (Name management — IPM-backed). Picking **Insured** shows a single free-text input. **Internal is intentionally excluded**: internal staff (adjuster/colleague) can register the claim but are never the notifier — the actual notifying party is always external.

Re-uses the existing FnolStepperComponent. Location capture is NOT its own step — see AC-06 — it lives on the Loss page, same placement as the regular happy-path flow.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Parties page starts empty, carries over the notifier broker, and supports adding another party — never mandatory
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The **Parties** page does *not* pre-populate from a policy — there is none for an orphan claim, so it starts empty except for the broker carried over from the notifier screen (if one was selected there). The user can **Add party** to cover cases like a different insurer reaching out about the claim. Parties are **not mandatory** — Next always works, same rule as the regular claim flow.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Location capture lives on the Loss page, GIS search + manual entry only — no 'select from contract location' option
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: Location capture is **not a separate step** (superseded 2026-09-11, Vasudha feedback — 'this does not require a separate page and can be captured on the Loss Information page itself, consistent with the regular FNOL flow'). It's a 'Locations of loss' card on the Loss page, same placement as the regular happy-path flow. 'Add location' opens a modal offering a GIS address search (type-ahead, independent of any policy — selecting a suggestion prefills the address fields) plus manual Address/Coordinates entry as a fallback. It cannot use the standard Location Manager MFE's contract-location search, because that depends on a linked policy, which does not exist for an orphan claim.

setup.description: Orphan path — Location card is on the Loss page, no separate step

preconditions.text: 'Add location' opens the manual-entry modal directly — no intermediate policy-location search step
Modal has a GIS 'Search location' field above the Address/Coordinates form; typing shows a dropdown of matching addresses

expectedUI.description: Same look-and-feel as the regular claim flow's location screen, minus the contract-location path, plus GIS search
visualCues: Section heading 'Locations of loss' on the Loss page, below General information
Empty state: 'Where did the loss occur?' + 'Add location' button

'Add location' → modal titled 'Add location manually' with a 'Search location' box at the top (GIS type-ahead) above the Address/Coordinates form (address line 1/2, postal code, city, country, province) and an 'Optional details' section for property ID + latitude/longitude
Selecting a GIS suggestion fills the address fields — the fields stay editable afterward
No policy-location search modal or 'select from contract' affordance anywhere on this card
Added location renders as a table row with Edit / Remove via kebab

howToTest.trigger: Click 'Add location', type into 'Search location' and pick a suggestion, or fill the manual-entry form directly (optionally expand 'Optional details' for coordinates), save
howToTest.expectedResult: Location appears as a row in the table; no contract/policy location option was ever shown
